shapes.name: OntologyCharter
shapes.description: One active charter per repo — the constitution of this repo's ontology. Singleton with a fixed, well-known name: ontology/charter, so any agent can fetch it in any repo without discovery. This charter binds only its own repo; cross-repo composition is expressed as dependencies (dependsOn), never membership.

mission.description: What this repo's ontology represents and for whom (the audience belongs in the mission; per-question personas live on the questions) — one paragraph a reviewer can test proposals against. Example: "Canonical identity and regulatory knowledge for US public water infrastructure — for the engineers, analysts, and agents who compose beliefs over it."

nonGoals.description: What this ontology deliberately is not. As load-bearing as the mission. Example: ["Utility finance and rates", "Hydraulic process modeling"]

commitments.description: Binding design rules (identity, epistemic, temporal, layering). A proposal that violates one requires an OntologyDecision, not a silent exception. Example: ["Evaluate established domain identities before minting alternatives; never assume or reject source identity categorically"]

dependsOn?.description: Upstream ontologies this repo composes over — each entry the canonical wref of an upstream release Set (preferred: pins the exact contract versions depended on, like a lockfile) or an upstream charter. Dependencies, never membership: this charter binds only its own repo. Example: [wh:pub/us.environmental.epa-npdes/ontology/release@v4]

shapes.name: CompetencyQuestion
shapes.description: A question the ontology must answer — the unit of scope, evaluation, and acceptance. The deletion test runs against these: a Shape no question cites does not ship. Naming: ontology/{domain}/{id}.

question.description: The question, phrased as its persona would actually ask it — including the decision it feeds, where that matters. Example: "Which NC wastewater facilities show recurring warm-season ammonia exceedances — and on what evidence?"

personas.description: Who asks it. Example: ["water-practice lead", "market analyst"]

requiredConcepts.description: The Shapes this question depends on — the deletion-test receipts. Example: [hub/shapes/Facility@v2, hub/shapes/Measurement@v3, hub/shapes/PermitLimit@v1, hub/shapes/PerformancePattern@v1]; use installed Shape versions

temporalSemantics?.description: Observation window, seasonality, as-of semantics the answer must honor. Example: "Warm season = May–Sep; windows 2022–2025; answer as-of latest complete quarter"

provenanceRequirement?.description: How deep the answer's pedigree must reach to count as answered. Example: artifact-hash-level

shapes.name: SemanticContract
shapes.description: Assertion, about a Shape this repo owns: the semantic contract governing a type, version-bound to the exact Shape revision it governs. Naming: ontology/{type}/semantic-contract; the suffix distinguishes it from the NamingContract for the same type. Which questions a type serves is not stored — it is the backlink query over CompetencyQuestion.requiredConcepts; never store what the graph already encodes.

definition.description: What the concept is, in domain language and, when adopted, the established authority's terms. Example: "A facility, site, or place of environmental interest identified under the reviewed EPA FRS contract"

identityTest.description: When do two records refer to the same one of these? The heart of the contract — most ontology failures are identity failures. Example: "Same EPA FRS Registry ID under the reviewed FRS lifecycle and correction rules"

examples?.description: Things that are this concept. Example: ["FRS Registry ID 110012345678"]

counterexamples?.description: Things that look like this concept and are not under the adopted authority contract. Example: ["A linked NPDES program record", "A permit held by the facility"]

lifecycleNotes?.description: How identity begins and ends, including adopted authority correction, merge, split, reuse, and succession behavior. Example: "Follow reviewed FRS correction, merge, and split semantics; display-name or program-link changes preserve identity"

lifecycleStatus.description: Contract maturity; consumers read this before depending. Example: approved

shapes.name: PredicateDeclaration
shapes.description: Assertion, about a predicate Shape this repo owns: the relationship's ontological metadata — everything a writer or reader needs that does not belong on the predicate Shape's field list. Naming: ontology/{predicate}, distinct from any NamingContract for that predicate. Whether instances carry valid time is visible from the predicate Shape's own fields; evidence expectations belong in that Shape's field constraints.

subjectPattern.description: Name-glob for the relationship subject (Arc from / first Bond end). Example: identity/organization/**

objectPattern.description: Name-glob for the relationship object (Arc to / second Bond end). Example: identity/facility/**

subjectForm.description: Directed (arc) or symmetric (bond) relationship subject. Example: arc

subjectNameRecipe?.description: Deterministic recipe for naming the Arc/Bond. The platform never converges independent writers; this recipe is what makes them mint one relationship subject instead of two. State what happens on member rename. Example: identity/rel/{subject-last-segment}--{object-last-segment} yielding identity/rel/epa-npdes-NC0071234--epa-frs-110012345678

structuralCardinality.description: Across all modeled history. Example: many:many

concurrentCardinality?.description: During overlapping valid time — a different question (joint ownership is real). Example: one:many

epistemicClass?.description: Which kind of claim this predicate makes. Never collapse the three into one Shape. Example: normalized-state

prohibitedSemantics?.description: Meanings this predicate must not be used for. Example: ["operation", "permitteeship"]

antiInferences?.description: The seductive shortcuts agents must not take. Put these where agents will read them. Example: ["permit-issued-to does not imply ownership"]

shapes.name: NamingContract
shapes.description: Assertion, about a Shape this repo owns: the namespace contract for that Shape's Things. Naming: ontology/{shape}, distinct from any other contract for that Shape.

nameTemplate.description: The name template for this Shape's Things. Example: identity/facility/epa-frs/{registry-id}

segmentSemantics.description: What each segment means and why it is where it is (leading segments = the dimensions agents narrow by; layer segment = cross-shape scoping). Example: ["identity — the layer; scopes globs and tokens", "facility — the Thing family", "epa-frs — adopted identity authority", "registry-id — authority-managed key"]

exampleNames.description: Enough real examples that an agent can infer the convention and predict nearby Things (depth included). Example: [identity/facility/epa-frs/110012345678]

globs?.description: The subtree selections this namespace is designed to serve — the same vocabulary scopes queries, subscriptions, tokens, and feeds. A rename updates these globs, nameTemplate, and exampleNames in the same migration. Example: [identity/facility/epa-frs/**, identity/**]

identityStabilityTest.description: Which real-world changes must NOT falsify a name. If an identity-preserving change breaks the name, the contract is wrong. No-relationships-in-names is a global rule, not per-shape configuration. Example: "FRS display-name, address, owner, and program-link changes must not break the Registry ID name; follow reviewed correction/split/merge semantics"

shapes.name: GoldenCase
shapes.description: An adversarial real-world case, pointing at the live data that models it — the fixture IS production data. The review question is always the same: is the ontology lying? Naming: ontology/{slug}.

title.description: The case in a phrase. Example: "Several program records, one FRS identity"

narrative.description: The real-world situation, precisely why it is adversarial (which identity test or cardinality assumption it attacks), and what passing looks like. Example: "Linked NPDES and state program records attack the temptation to mint private facilities. Passing: both resolve to the authority-managed FRS identity while their source claims remain distinct."

exemplarWrefs.description: The live Things and Assertions modeling this case. Example: [identity/facility/epa-frs/110012345678, identity/refers-to-facility/epa-npdes/NC0071234]

shapes.name: OntologyDecision
shapes.description: A deliberately open or explicitly resolved design decision. Unresolved-on-purpose beats silently-inconsistent. Naming: ontology/od-{id}.

title.description: The decision in a phrase. Example: "Pump stations: Facilities or components?"

question.description: What is actually being decided. Example: "Do pump stations get their own Facility identity, or ride as components of the works they feed?"

options.description: The candidate answers, with their trade-offs. Example: ["Own Facility (can hold permits)", "Component of parent works"]

currentLean?.description: The working position, if any. Example: "Own Facility"

settlingEvidence?.description: What observation or experiment would settle it — the decision's exit criteria. Example: "Whether any NC pump station holds its own NPDES permit"

resolution?.description: The answer and its rationale, once resolved.

shapes.name: CompetencyEvaluation
shapes.description: Assertion, about a CompetencyQuestion: the claim that a specific release answers a specific question. Binomial and attributed — independent evaluators may disagree, and Veritas consensus over evaluations is meaningful. Evaluation is ex-post by construction: revise contracts, revise the ontology/release Set (a new release), then evaluate against it. A failing evaluation is not a blocked release; the gate is on adoption, not on release. Naming: ontology/{release-version}/{question}.

release.description: The release evaluated — ontology/release pinned to the version under test (this field is version-bound; author the exact evaluated release pin). Backlinks make all-evaluations-of-release-N one query. Example: ontology/release@v3

passed.description: Did the release answer the question within its provenance requirements? Example: true

evaluator.description: The agent or human who ran the evaluation and stands behind it. Example: evaluate-ontology/1.2 (agent)

evaluatedAsOf.description: ISO timestamp of the evaluation run. Example: 2026-07-01T04:00:00Z

queryExecuted.description: The concrete query or traversal used — the evaluation must be reproducible. Example: "reverse-about: PerformancePattern water/performance-pattern/** where patternClass=recurring-warm-season-elevation, joined to Facility"

resultDigest?.description: Short digest of the result that satisfied (or failed) the question. Example: "14 facilities; every pattern traverses to a DMR artifact hash"

notes?.description: Scale caveats, cohort scope, re-run triggers. Example: "NC cohort only; re-run when a new DMR quarter lands"
